title: indian shares set modest gains mideast tensions keep investors wary 2026 09 07
text:
Sept 7 (Reuters) - Indian shares dipped on Monday after posting four consecutive weekly declines, with IT stocks leading a broad-based ​selloff as escalating tensions in the Middle East and rising odds of a ‌U.S. rate hike in September weighed on risk sentiment.
The Nifty 50 (.NSEI)
, opens new tab
 slipped 0.25% to 23,838.65 and the BSE Sensex (.BSESN)
, opens new tab
 shed 0.24% to 76,335.07 by 9:46 a.m. IST.
Fourteen of ​the 16 major sectors logged losses.
IT index (.NIFTYIT)
, opens new tab
 fell about 2% after ​stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs growth data boosted bets of a September ⁠interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve.
Higher U.S. rates could curb client ​spending, weighing on Indian IT firms that generate a significant share of their ​revenue from the United States.
Broader small-caps (.NIFSMCP100)
, opens new tab
 and mid-caps (.NIFMDCP100)
, opens new tab
 fell 0.2% each as rising crude prices and escalating U.S.-Iran tensions dented risk appetite.
"Global cues are likely to continue dominating market ​sentiment this week, with U.S. inflation data later this week closely watched ​ahead of the Fed policy meeting on September 16," said Santosh Meena, head of research ‌at ⁠Swastika Investmart.
"Another key factor will be the U.S-Iran situation, as renewed tensions could push crude prices higher, while a record number of IPOs hitting the street could keep India's secondary market subdued," Meena said.
Among stocks, Zee Entertainment (ZEE.NS)
, opens new tab
 fell ​4% after India's ​premier investigating agency ⁠filed an FIR against Essel Group Chair Subhash Chandra and some other individuals for allegedly defrauding LIC Housing Finance.
Indoco ​Remedies (INRM.NS)
, opens new tab
 lost 3% after the U.S. drug regulator completed ​its inspection ⁠at the pharma company's Goa manufacturing facility and issued seven form 483 observations. Form 483 flags conditions that violate U.S. standards.
PVR Inox (PVRL.NS)
, opens new tab
 slid 6.5% after the ⁠Economic Times ​reported that the multiplex operator asked a ​senior executive to leave in April following an internal probe into alleged kickbacks from developers building ​its cinema properties.
